statement: "If This Was a Movie" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift from the deluxe edition of her third studio album Speak Now (2010).
Taylor Swift wrote the track with Martin Johnson and produced it with Nathan Chapman.
"If This Was a Movie" is a fast-paced pop rock ballad.
"If This Was a Movie" includes both acoustic and electric string instruments, drums, key notes, and full orchestration.
In the lyrics of "If This Was a Movie", Swift's character begs an ex-lover to return to her and expects him to do so like it was a movie.
Big Machine Records released "If This Was a Movie" digitally through the iTunes Store on November 8, 2011.
The song reached charts in Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
The song debuted within the top ten of the Billboard Hot 100 in the United States.
Two publication reviews of the track were published in late 2011.
One review found the track engaging.
The other review deemed that the track showcased newfound maturity within Swift's lyrics.
Retrospective rankings of Swift's songs have included "If This Was a Movie" within the lower-tier positions.
On March 17, 2023, Swift released a re-recording of the song, titled "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)", alongside three other songs to streaming services.
The re-recording was released in celebration of the start of her Eras Tour.
Swift debuted "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" live on piano during a Minneapolis show on June 23.
The re-recording was part of an effort to re-record her early catalog after a dispute over the ownership of the master recordings.
Taylor Swift conceived her third studio album, Speak Now (2010), as a collection of tracks about the things she had wanted to say but was unable to do with the people she had met.
As many as 25 songs were written by Swift for the album Speak Now.
Swift co-produced Speak Now with Nathan Chapman, who had worked on her previous releases.
By around mid-2010, Swift had secured the final track list for Speak Now.
All the tracks on the final track list for Speak Now were written by Swift, with the exception of "If This Was a Movie".
"If This Was a Movie" was written by Swift with Martin Johnson alongside other songs.
"If This Was a Movie" was included as a bonus track in Speak Now's deluxe edition.
Speak Now's deluxe edition was released as a Target-exclusive alongside the standard edition on October 25, 2010.
Big Machine Records made "If This Was a Movie" digitally available, along with the other bonus tracks, through the iTunes Store on November 8, 2011.
On June 23, 2023, Swift debuted the track live on piano during a show in Minneapolis, as part of her Eras Tour (2023–2024).
"If This Was a Movie" was produced by Swift and Chapman.
"If This Was a Movie" is a pop rock ballad that critics described as "somber" and "sparkling".
The song "If This Was a Movie" is set on a fast pace.
"If This Was a Movie" has a length of 5 minutes and 48 seconds.
According to the Seattle Weekly's Erin Thompson, the song has a basic arrangement and structure, which he regarded as "Swiftian".
"If This Was a Movie" features acoustic string instruments from country and folk music, an electric guitar amplified by distortion, and full orchestration.
The musicologist James E. Perone said that this arrangement could give "mixed-genre messages" to listeners.
A simple, recurring guitar riff is played throughout "If This Was a Movie".
Drums and key notes lead Swift in "If This Was a Movie".
The verse's melody in "If This Was a Movie" is performed at a low register and built on short motive figures.
The dramatic chorus in "If This Was a Movie", where Swift sings with a twang accompanied by harmonies, contrasts the verse by being more melodious and performed at a higher register.
In the lyrics of "If This Was a Movie", Swift's character pleads an ex-lover, who had left for six months, to come back to her, expecting him to do as such like it was a movie.
Swift's character imagines that through this perspective, her ex-lover would be sorry to her for what mistake he made, and she would accept his apology and reconcile with him.
A staff from Billboard said that Swift was in a state of coming of age in the lyrics of "If This Was a Movie".
The Billboard staff believed that Swift departs from the "fantasy world of high school" and examines "more mature content" in the lyrics of "If This Was a Movie".
Swift often recalls the important memories when she and her ex-lover were together in the song.
"If This Was a Movie" includes a lyric about being in the rain ("Stand in the rain/'Til I came out").
Erin Thompson felt the lyric about being in the rain was used extensively in Swift's songs.
By the conclusion of "If This Was a Movie", the ideal ending does not happen like Swift had hoped for.
In late 2011, two publication reviews of "If This Was a Movie" were issued.
Erin Thompson included "If This Was a Movie" in the Seattle Weekly's "Nice Hits!"—a column that explores the best tracks out of the top 40 songs in a given time.

Thompson believed that while not "lyrically perfect", the track had the features that made Swift's songs engaging, including for what he considered vulnerable, relatable songwriting and a simple composition.
Billboard's staff stated that "If This Was a Movie" showcased "a more age-appropriate track" from Swift.
Over the years, retrospective rankings of Swift's songs have included "If This Was a Movie" within the lower-tier positions.
Paste's ranking, published in February 2020, listed "If This Was a Movie" as 115th among Swift's 158 songs.
One of Paste's writers, Jane Song, took issue with the line, "Come back to me like", which she heard as "Come back to me, daylight".
In her September 2020 ranking of Swift's 161 tracks for NME, Hannah Mylrea placed the song at 150th.
Hannah Mylrea wrote that "it stutters towards the finish line" and that it was "frustratingly repetitive" overall.
Rob Sheffield listed the track as 266th in his October 2025 ranking of Swift's 286 songs for Rolling Stone.
The next month, Nate Jones of Vulture updated his ranking of Swift's 245 tracks, where the song was placed at 170th.
Nate Jones viewed "If This Was a Movie" as "the mirror image" of Swift's track "White Horse" (2008) that, to him, made it "oddly superfluous".
Carena Liptak of Taste of Country included the song as 16th in her 2023 ranking of all 17 original tracks from Speak Now's deluxe edition.

Carena Liptak said that "If This Was a Movie", while not among the album's most memorable, displayed "Swift's heartbreak songwriting at its wistful, earworm-y best" and that its emotional impact was skillfully handled.
Carena Liptak attributed the placement to how other tracks better showcase Swift's "ability to wax poetic on heartbreak and nostalgia".
After its digital release in November 2011, "If This Was a Movie" debuted at number ten on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in the United States.
The track "If This Was a Movie" reached number three on Digital Songs in the United States with 163,000 downloads.
The top-ten entry on the Hot 100 made "If This Was a Movie" the fourth track from Speak Now to do so.
The top-ten entry on the Hot 100 extended Swift's record of most top-ten debuts for any act with ten.
"If This Was a Movie" peaked atop on Country Digital Song Sales.
The song "If This Was a Movie" reached number 191 in the United Kingdom.
The song "If This Was a Movie" reached number 17 in Canada.
The song "If This Was a Movie" peaked at number 10 on Canada Digital Song Sales.

To celebrate the start of the Eras Tour on March 17, 2023, Swift released a re-recording of the song, titled "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)", on that day alongside three other songs to streaming services.
The re-recording "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" was also part of an attempt to re-record her early catalog after a dispute over the ownership of the master recordings.
"If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" has the same cover art as that of Swift's re-recorded album, Fearless (Taylor's Version) (2021).
"If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" was included on the compilation, The More Fearless (Taylor's Version) Chapter, which was also released on March 17, 2023.
Speculation ensued amongst fans regarding the song's release, according to some journalists.
Journalists questioned whether "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" would be featured on Speak Now's re-recording, Speak Now (Taylor's Version) (2023).
When Speak Now (Taylor's Version)'s track list was unveiled on June 5, 2023, the song was not on it.
"If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" has a length of 3 minutes and 57 seconds.
The Times's Will Hodgkinson described "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" as "straightforward, innocent, slightly breathy balladry with an orchestral backing".
"If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" was produced by Swift and its vocal engineer Christopher Rowe.
Amos Heller played bass on "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
David Cook played piano on "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
Matt Billingslea played drums and percussion on "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
Max Bernstein played electric guitar on "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
Max Bernstein also provided synthesizer programming on "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
Mike Meadows played acoustic guitar on "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
Mike Meadows was the background vocalist on "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
Paul Sidoti played electric guitar on "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
The engineers for "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" were Bryce Bordone and Derek Garten.
Derek Garten was also the editor alongside Lowell Reynolds for "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
David Payne was the recording engineer for "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
David Payne was assisted by Lowell Reynolds for "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)".
The mixer for "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" was Serban Ghenea.
The mastering engineer for "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" was Randy Merrill.
In two reviews of the four songs that were released right before the start of Swift's Eras Tour, "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" received favorable comments.
Writing for The Freeman, Januar Junior Aguja said that "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" could have new fans because of Swift's vocals on the re-recording.
Januar Junior Aguja claimed that Swift's vocals on the re-recording had improved.
Will Hodgkinson wrote that the song "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" was "corny but smart".
Will Hodgkinson stated that "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" had Swift's early brilliance of "capturing an entire romantic drama in three minutes".
Will Hodgkinson considered that "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" had both an "ingenue spirit" and professionally-written ruthlessness.
Commercially, "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" reached number two on the Bubbling Under Hot 100 in the US.
"If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" reached number four on Digital Songs in the US with 11,300 downloads.
On Country Digital Song Sales, "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" became Swift's record-extending 19th number-one entry.
"If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" made "If This Was a Movie" the first song to have two versions peak atop the Country Digital Song Sales chart.
On sales-component charts in other countries, "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" reached number seven on Canada Digital Song Sales.
"If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" reached number thirteen on both UK Singles Downloads and UK Singles Sales.
"If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" entered at number twelve on Hot 40 Singles in New Zealand.
